n: The eighth and final vision: four chariots coming out between two bronze mountains — perhaps the gateway of heaven.
The first chariot has red horses, the second black.
The third has white horses, the fourth dappled ones.
They are the four spirits (or winds) of heaven, going out after standing before the Lord of all the earth — His agents carrying out His will everywhere.

f.w: the four spirits of the heavens

n: The black horses head north, with the white following; the dappled head south.

f.g: Babylon and Mesopotamia — reached from Israel by a northern route.

n: The strong horses are eager to go throughout the earth, and they are sent to patrol it.

f.w: walk to and fro through the earth

n: The Lord says those going north have given His Spirit rest there — His judgment on Babylon is accomplished.

f.g: Settled My anger — satisfied My justice.

n: After the visions, a new message from the Lord comes with a symbolic action.

f.w: the word of the LORD came unto me

n: Zechariah is to receive gifts from three returned exiles — Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah — and go to Josiah’s house.

f.g: Exiles who had returned from Babylon, bringing donations.

n: With the silver and gold he is to make crowns and place one on Joshua the high priest’s head — a surprising act, since crowns belonged to kings, not priests.

f.g: Hebrew plural, perhaps an ornate crown with several circlets.

n: “Behold the man whose name is the Branch.” He will grow up from his place and build the Lord’s temple. The Branch is a messianic title; Pilate’s words “Behold the man!” echo this phrase.
The Branch will build the temple, bear royal glory, and rule as both king and priest on his throne — two roles united. Christians see this fulfilled in Jesus, our King and High Priest.

f.w: he shall be a priest upon his throne
the counsel of peace shall be between them both
f.g: Harmony between the royal and priestly offices.

n: The crown will be kept in the temple as a memorial honoring the donors.
People from far away will come help build the temple. This will happen — if they diligently obey the Lord. God’s promises are tied to obedience.

f.w: they that are far off shall come
